name: LinguaGapAtlas
description: Structured corpus of 96 multilingual AI resources (65 benchmarks and 31 datasets, 2018-2025) classified on five taxonomy dimensions - data origin, linguistic resource tier, task class, cultural specificity, and inference paradigm - with per-resource provenance, the 142-candidate screening log, the annotation codebook, and scripts that recompute the paper's headline statistics and inter-annotator agreement.
citeAs: Jajee, S. K., Shaw, T., & Soni, V. LinguaGapAtlas: A Corpus and Taxonomy of 96 Multilingual AI Benchmarks and Datasets (corpus and reproducibility package, v1.0.0). https://github.com/sankalpjajee/LinguaGapAtlas

distribution.name: linguagapatlas.jsonl
distribution.description: One resource per line: consensus labels, votes and the five rounds.

distribution.name: linguagapatlas.json
distribution.description: The whole atlas as one JSON document (metadata, taxonomy, statistics, caveats and all resources).

distribution.name: linguagapatlas.sqlite
distribution.description: The same content as SQLite tables and views.

recordSet.name: resources
recordSet.description: The 96 resources with their consensus labels (null = undetermined).

field.name: resource_id
field.description: Stable ID assigned by this project, form QG-001…QG-096. Never reused, never renumbered between versions.

field.name: resource_name
field.description: The resource's canonical name as given by its creators (e.g. the benchmark/dataset name used in its paper).

field.name: canonical_reference
field.description: Full citation (authors, title, venue, year) of the paper or release that introduces the resource. null if the resource has no citable paper.

field.name: type
field.description: Benchmark or Dataset. Benchmarks are resources designed for evaluation; datasets are resources designed primarily for training. A resource released as both is coded by its primary stated purpose and the dual nature is noted in evidence_note.

field.name: year
field.description: Year of first public release (paper or public artifact, whichever came first). null if not determinable.

field.name: languages
field.description: Semicolon-separated list of language names (or ISO 639 codes) the resource covers, as documented by its creators. null if the documentation does not enumerate them.

field.name: language_names
field.description: Derived from `languages`: the entries that name a language, in source order (entries such as '75 languages' that only state a count are left out). null when `languages` is null.

field.name: languages_fully_named
field.description: true when `language_names` names every covered language: no count-only entries and as many names as `language_count`.

field.name: language_count
field.description: Number of languages covered, counted from languages where enumerated, otherwise the count stated by the creators. null if neither is available. Never estimated.

field.name: data_origin
field.description: How the resource's content was produced. Native: authored originally in the target language(s). Translated: produced by translating content from another language (human or machine). Mixed: both routes used for substantial portions. null if the production route is not documented.

field.name: resource_tier
field.description: Linguistic resource tier of the language(s) the resource targets, per the paper's tiering of language resourcedness. For multilingual resources, the tier of the lowest-resourced language substantially covered. null if the covered languages cannot be established.

field.name: task_class
field.description: The task family the resource evaluates or supports. Benchmarks: QA, Syntax, Reasoning, Multimodal, NLU, Summarization, Math, RAG, Code, Other. Datasets: Pre-training, Translation, Instruction. A resource spanning several classes is coded by its primary class; secondary classes go in evidence_note.

field.name: cultural_specificity
field.description: Universal: designed to be culturally non-specific. Culturally Anchored: content is grounded in the cultural context of its language community without being tied to one sub-region. Region-Specific: content is grounded in a particular country/region's context. null if the documentation does not support a judgement.

field.name: inference_paradigm
field.description: The inference/evaluation paradigm the resource is built around. Vocabulary to be confirmed against the final codebook before v1.0.0; rows coded before confirmation carry the coder's best judgement and are flagged in confidence. null if not determinable.

field.name: provenance_url
field.description: The evidence source the row's labels were taken from — the resource's paper, repository, or documentation page actually consulted. Every coded dimension in the row must be supported by this source or by evidence_note. null only for rows with no coded dimensions.

field.name: evidence_note
field.description: Free-text note recording what the source states that supports the labels (quoted or paraphrased), plus any dual-nature or secondary-class remarks. This is the audit trail for the row.

field.name: coder
field.description: Identifier of the coder who produced this row's labels (initials or coder ID used in the reliability study).

field.name: confidence
field.description: Coder's confidence in the row's labels: high, medium, or low. low rows are candidates for adjudication and are reported as such. null if not recorded.

field.name: screening_status
field.description: Disposition of this resource in the screening pipeline (see data/screening-log.csv): for rows in corpus.csv this is always included; the full candidate set, including exclusions, lives in the screening log.

field.name: screening_reason
field.description: For included rows, the eligibility basis (e.g. which inclusion criterion the resource met). Exclusion reasons are recorded in the screening log, not here.

recordSet.description: Each coding round's record for each resource (5 per resource).
